title: Being super-rich
paragraphs: Do you consider yourself wealthy? Do you have enough cash in the bank to have no financial worries? Or maybe, like me, being rich is just something you can only dream about? For most of us, the most likely way to become a millionaire is to win the lottery, but without buying a ticket, what other ways are there to get super- rich?

A ‘super-rich‘ person is often defined as someone with over $30 million dollars of assets - so it’s not just about having a suitcase stuffed full of banknotes! They usually own property, an expensive yacht or eat in swanky restaurants. And there appear to be more and more of these people, as it‘s reported that the number of super- rich is expected to increase by 43% over the next decade.

If you save your pennies, make the right investments and work hard, could you be one of them? It’s unlikely because a report last year highlighted inequality in the world, saying the richest 62 individuals owned as much as the poorest 50%. But for those lucky ones who are loaded, what is it that they splash the cash on?

One academic in the UK, Emma Spence, has been researching just that - and her answer is yachts! It‘s the ultimate status symbol but she also says “a superyacht is essentially a black hole of wealth” - in other words, it continually eats your money and doesn’t increase in value like an art collection might.

But if you‘ve got the spare cash, why not have one! It’s an excuse to show off your wealth and position in society. Interestingly, Emma Spence found that the size of someone‘s yacht shows their place in the pecking order. This is a good example of conspicuous consumption - buying something so someone else notices.

In the past you may have expected to find a super- rich, yacht- owning, billionaire to live in developed countries like the USA but now the wealthy can be found hanging out in most corners of the world. According to a report by Knight Frank, Vietnam is the country expected to have the fastest growth of super- rich over the next 10 years - an amazing 170% increase.

If all this makes you feel poor, remember that being wealthy doesn‘t necessarily make you happy. You don’t have to waste time worrying about what to spend your money on. And you can feel rich in other ways by having good friends and family, good health or just a happy life - things that don‘t cost the earth. And if you really want a yacht, how about a toy one to play with in the bath?! How rich do you feel today?

vocabulary.entry: assets [n. pl.] /ˈæsets/ 资产；财产 (书面语；单数: asset)
vocabulary.example: The company has assets of over $1 million.
vocabulary.translation: 这家公司拥有超过100万美元的资产。

vocabulary.entry: swanky [adj.] /ˈswæŋki/ 豪华的；阔气的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: They had dinner at a swanky restaurant.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在一家豪华餐厅吃了晚饭。

vocabulary.entry: inequality [n.] /ˌɪnɪˈkwɒləti/ 不平等；不均等 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The report focuses on income inequality.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告关注收入不平等。

vocabulary.entry: loaded [adj.] /ˈləʊdɪd/ 富有的；有钱的 (口语；俚语)
vocabulary.example: His uncle is loaded and owns several houses.
vocabulary.translation: 他的叔叔很有钱，拥有好几套房子。

vocabulary.entry: splash the cash [phr.] /splæʃ ðə kæʃ/ 挥霍金钱；大手大脚花钱 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He splashed the cash on a new sports car.
vocabulary.translation: 他花大钱买了一辆新跑车。

vocabulary.entry: ultimate [adj.] /ˈʌltɪmət/ 终极的；最终的 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: Winning the championship was his ultimate goal.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得冠军是他的终极目标。

vocabulary.entry: status symbol [n.] /ˈsteɪtəs ˌsɪmbəl/ 身份象征
vocabulary.example: A luxury watch is often seen as a status symbol.
vocabulary.translation: 豪华手表常被视为身份象征。

vocabulary.entry: pecking order [n.] /ˈpekɪŋ ɔːdə/ 等级秩序；社会地位排序 (口语；比喻)
vocabulary.example: New employees quickly learn the office pecking order.
vocabulary.translation: 新员工很快就能了解办公室的等级秩序。

vocabulary.entry: conspicuous consumption [n.] /kənˌspɪkjuəs kənˈsʌmpʃən/ 炫耀性消费 (书面语；专业术语)
vocabulary.example: Buying designer clothes is a form of conspicuous consumption.
vocabulary.translation: 购买名牌服装是一种炫耀性消费。

vocabulary.entry: don‘t cost the earth [phr.] /dəʊnt kɒst ði ɜːθ/ 价格不贵；花费不多 (口语)
vocabulary.example: A nice meal at home doesn’t cost the earth.
vocabulary.translation: 在家吃顿好的花不了多少钱。

vocabulary.entry: millionaire [n.] /ˌmɪljəˈneə/ 百万富翁
vocabulary.example: He became a millionaire by the age of 30.
vocabulary.translation: 他30岁时成为了百万富翁。

vocabulary.entry: lottery [n.] /ˈlɒtəri/ 彩票
vocabulary.example: She won the lottery and bought a new house.
vocabulary.translation: 她中了彩票，买了新房子。

vocabulary.entry: super-rich [adj.] /ˌsuːpə ˈrɪtʃ/ 超级富有的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: The super-rich family owns a private jet.
vocabulary.translation: 这个超级富豪家庭拥有一架私人飞机。

vocabulary.entry: banknotes [n. pl.] /ˈbæŋknəʊts/ 纸币；钞票 (单数: banknote)
vocabulary.example: He pulled a wad of banknotes from his pocket.
vocabulary.translation: 他从口袋里掏出一叠钞票。

vocabulary.entry: property [n.] /ˈprɒpəti/ 房产；财产
vocabulary.example: She owns property in London and Paris.
vocabulary.translation: 她在伦敦和巴黎都有房产。

vocabulary.entry: yacht [n.] /jɒt/ 游艇
vocabulary.example: They spent the weekend on their friend‘s yacht.
vocabulary.translation: 他们在朋友的游艇上度了周末。

vocabulary.entry: decade [n.] /ˈdekeɪd/ 十年
vocabulary.example: Technology has advanced rapidly over the past decade.
vocabulary.translation: 过去十年科技发展迅速。

vocabulary.entry: investments [n. pl.] /ɪnˈvestmənts/ 投资 (单数: investment)
vocabulary.example: He made wise investments in the stock market.
vocabulary.translation: 他在股票市场上做了明智的投资。

vocabulary.entry: billionaire [n.] /ˌbɪljəˈneə/ 亿万富翁
vocabulary.example: The billionaire donated millions to charity.
vocabulary.translation: 这位亿万富翁向慈善机构捐赠了数百万。

vocabulary.entry: developed countries [n. pl.] /dɪˌveləpt ˈkʌntriz/ 发达国家 (单数: developed country)
vocabulary.example: Most developed countries have universal healthcare.
vocabulary.translation: 大多数发达国家都有全民医保。

vocabulary.entry: spare cash [n.] /speə kæʃ/ 闲钱；多余的现金 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I don‘t have any spare cash this month.
vocabulary.translation: 我这个月没有闲钱。

vocabulary.entry: show off [phr.] /ʃəʊ ɒf/ 炫耀；卖弄 (口语)
vocabulary.example: He likes to show off his new car.
vocabulary.translation: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。

vocabulary.entry: academic [n.] /ˌækəˈdemɪk/ 学者 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The conference was attended by leading academics.
vocabulary.translation: 这次会议有顶尖学者参加。

vocabulary.entry: essentially [adv.] /ɪˈsenʃəli/ 本质上；基本上
vocabulary.example: The two methods are essentially the same.
vocabulary.translation: 这两种方法本质上是一样的。

vocabulary.entry: art collection [n.] /ˈɑːt kəˌlekʃən/ 艺术品收藏
vocabulary.example: His art collection is worth millions.
vocabulary.translation: 他的艺术品收藏价值数百万。

sentences.chinese: 或者，也许像我一样，富有仅仅是你只能梦想的事情？

sentences.english: They usually own property, an expensive yacht or eat in swanky restaurants.
sentences.chinese: 他们通常拥有房产、昂贵的游艇，或者在豪华餐厅用餐。

sentences.chinese: 而且这类人似乎越来越多，有报道称，未来十年超级富豪的数量预计将增加43%。

sentences.english: If you save your pennies, make the right investments and work hard, could you be one of them?
sentences.chinese: 如果你省吃俭用、正确地投资并努力工作，能成为他们中的一员吗？

sentences.chinese: 可能性不大，因为去年一份报告强调了全球的不平等现象，称最富有的62个人拥有的财富相当于最贫穷的50%人口的总和。

sentences.chinese: 但对于那些幸运的富豪来说，他们会把钱花在什么上面呢？

sentences.chinese: 英国学者艾玛·斯彭斯一直在研究这个问题——她的答案是游艇！

sentences.chinese: 游艇是终极身份象征，但她也表示“超级游艇本质上是财富黑洞”，换句话说，它会持续消耗你的钱，而且不会像艺术品收藏那样升值。

sentences.english: But if you‘ve got the spare cash, why not have one!
sentences.chinese: 但如果你有闲钱，为什么不买一艘呢？

sentences.english: It’s an excuse to show off your wealth and position in society.
sentences.chinese: 这是一个炫耀财富和社会地位的理由。

sentences.english: Interestingly, Emma Spence found that the size of someone‘s yacht shows their place in the pecking order.
sentences.chinese: 有趣的是，艾玛·斯彭斯发现，游艇的大小能体现一个人在等级体系中的地位。

sentences.english: This is a good example of conspicuous consumption - buying something so someone else notices.
sentences.chinese: 这是“炫耀性消费”的典型例子——购买某样东西就是为了让别人注意到。

sentences.chinese: 过去，你可能会认为拥有游艇、超级富有的亿万富翁会住在像美国这样的发达国家，但现在在世界大多数角落都能看到富豪的身影。

sentences.english: According to a report by Knight Frank, Vietnam is the country expected to have the fastest growth of super- rich over the next 10 years - an amazing 170% increase.

sentences.chinese: 如果这些让你觉得自己贫穷，记住，富有不一定能让你快乐。

sentences.chinese: 你不必花时间纠结该把钱花在哪里。

sentences.chinese: 而且你还可以通过拥有亲密的朋友和家人、健康的身体，或者仅仅是幸福的生活来感受“富有”——这些都无需花费巨额财富。

sentences.english: And if you really want a yacht, how about a toy one to play with in the bath?!
sentences.chinese: 如果你真的想要一艘游艇，买个能在浴缸里玩的玩具游艇怎么样？

sentences.english: How rich do you feel today?
sentences.chinese: 今天的你觉得自己有多“富有”呢？
